description: What an agent is doing right now, in the one vocabulary every agent visualization shares. The state is always painted three ways at once — a tone colour, an icon and a localized WORD — because a colour alone is not information a colour-blind or screen-reader reader can use (WCAG 1.4.1); the icon and the word come from the AI package's shared AgentStatusPresentation mapping, so a lane, a graph node and a fan-out tile cannot disagree about what "running" looks like. The set is transport-neutral: a host maps its own backend vocabulary (a queued turn, a leased attempt, a permission wait, a finished run) onto these seven values and the visualizations stay backend-free.

members.name: Idle
members.description: The agent exists but has nothing to do. The neutral state, and the one an unknown backend value falls back to.

members.name: Queued
members.description: Work is assigned to the agent and it has not started yet — a turn in the queue, a task waiting for a free slot.

members.name: Running
members.description: The agent is working right now. The only state whose duration is still growing.

members.name: WaitingForApproval
members.description: The agent stopped and is waiting for a human decision (an approval, a permission grant, a review verdict). Painted in the attention tone, because nothing moves until the reader acts.

members.name: Succeeded
members.description: The agent finished its work successfully. A terminal state.

members.name: Failed
members.description: The agent failed. A terminal state; the failure reason belongs to the host's own data.

members.name: Cancelled
members.description: The agent was stopped before it finished. Terminal, and neither a success nor a failure.
